technique.how: Inspect the skin around the knees in good light. Score 0 = no mottling; 1 = coin-sized area on the patella; 2 = does not exceed the superior edge of the kneecap; 3 = does not exceed the middle of the thigh; 4 = does not exceed the groin fold; 5 = beyond the groin fold. Score the worse leg and repeat after resuscitation (e.g. at 6 h).
technique.prerequisites: Legs uncovered and warm room; assess after initial resuscitation as in the source studies. Scoring is unreliable in dark skin and in local vascular disease of the leg.

interpretation.positive_finding: Mottling score 2-3 or 4-5 after initial resuscitation in septic shock is strongly associated with 14-day death (OR 16 and 74 vs score 0-1); pooled sepsis data confirm association with 28-day mortality (OR 2.27).
interpretation.negative_finding: Absent or minimal mottling (score 0-1), or a score that falls during resuscitation, identifies a lower-risk group (14-day mortality 12% vs 77% when the score decreased vs not).
interpretation.pitfalls: This is a prognostic marker, not a diagnostic test for the cause of shock; it is not assessable in dark skin, and peripheral vascular disease, cold exposure or vasopressor-induced vasoconstriction can mottle the skin.
interpretation.changes_what: A high or rising mottling score should prompt escalation of perfusion-targeted resuscitation and senior/ICU review, independent of MAP or lactate.

sources.citation: Ait-Oufella H, Lemoinne S, Boelle PY, et al. Mottling score predicts survival in septic shock. Intensive Care Med. 2011;37(5):801-807.

Shi LJ, Ke SF, Fu LS, et al. Meta-analysis of the prognostic value of skin perfusion parameters in sepsis patients: evidence integration based on the mottling score, capillary refill time, and peripheral perfusion index. Shock. 2026.

Dumas G, Lavillegrand JR, Joffre J, et al. Mottling score is a strong predictor of 14-day mortality in septic patients whatever vasopressor doses and other tissue perfusion parameters. Crit Care. 2019;23(1):211.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Not assessable in dark skin (excluded from the source studies) or with severe peripheral arterial disease of the legs; does not identify the cause of shock.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Score 4-5, or a score that persists or rises after 6 h of resuscitation, carries very high short-term mortality and warrants immediate ICU-level escalation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Excellent agreement between independent observers, kappa 0.87 (95% CI 0.72-0.97) in Ait-Oufella 2011.

extraction_notes: No sensitivity/specificity/LR for the mottling score were found, so estimates=[] and evidence_status is not_quantified; the evidence is prognostic odds ratios, recorded here with quotes. Ait-Oufella 2011 (PMID 21373821), 60 septic shock patients, ICU, 14-day mortality 45%, Abstract Results: 'mottling score [score 0-1 OR 1; score 2-3 OR 16, 95% CI (4-81); score 4-5 OR 74, 95% CI (11-1,568), p < 0.0001]'. Shi 2026 Shock meta-analysis (PMID 42258324), 22 studies n=2,727, Abstract Results: 'MS was significantly associated with 28-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) = 2.27, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.79-2.87, P < 0.001]'. Dumas 2019 (PMID 31182133, PMC6558704 full text), 259 sepsis/septic shock patients, Table 2: 'Mottling score at H6, by point 2.26 [1.72-2.97]' (adjusted OR per point, 14-day mortality). The score is a prognostic marker in shock; the seeded differentials are retained but it does not discriminate between them.
